questions.stem_en: A company created an account-level subscription filter policy that sends all log groups to Amazon Data Firehose for central processing. Soon afterward, CloudWatch Logs ingestion charges rose sharply because log groups that receive logs from the delivery workflow's own resources were also being subscribed, causing a recursive loop. Which change will MOST effectively stop the loop while keeping the central processing?

choices_en.text: Add selection criteria to the account-level policy that exclude log groups which ingest logs from resources in the delivery workflow.
Increase the Firehose buffer size and buffer interval so that fewer deliveries are made.
Delete the account-level policy and ask each team to create its own log group subscription filters.
Turn on decompression in Firehose so that the logs are smaller when they are delivered.

explanation.summary: サブスクリプションフィルターでは、再帰のループが起きて取り込みの料金が大きく増えることがあります。これを防ぐには、アカウントレベルのサブスクリプションフィルターの選択の条件で、配信の仕組みに含まれるリソースからログを取り込むロググループを除外することが勧められています。

per_choice.A: 正しい。ループのもとになるロググループだけを外し、ほかのロググループの中央の処理は続けられます。
per_choice.B: 配信の回数は減っても、ループで取り込まれるログの量は減りません。
per_choice.C: ループは止まりますが、中央でまとめて処理する仕組みが崩れ、各チームの手間が増えます。
per_choice.D: 解凍してもループは止まらず、取り込みの料金も減りません。

references.quote: There is a risk of causing an infinite recursive loop with subscription filters that can lead to a large increase in ingestion billing if not addressed.
we recommend that you use selection criteria in your account-level subscription filters to exclude log groups that ingest log data from resources that are part of the subscription delivery workflow.

questions.stem_en: A team wants to stream logs from a CloudWatch Logs log group to an Amazon OpenSearch Service domain that uses VPC access. The streaming setup uses a Lambda function that writes to the domain, but the function cannot reach the domain endpoint. Which actions should a DevOps engineer take to make the streaming work? (Choose TWO.)

choices_en.text: Use a Lambda execution role that trusts lambda.amazonaws.com and has the AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole policy attached.
Make sure that the source log group uses the Standard log class.
Change the existing OpenSearch Service domain from VPC access to public access.
Turn on gzip compression for the subscription so that the data fits through the VPC.
Add logs.amazonaws.com to the trust relationship of the Lambda execution role instead of lambda.amazonaws.com.

explanation.summary: OpenSearch Service へ流す時、Lambda の実行ロールは信頼関係に lambda.amazonaws.com を持つ必要があり、VPC アクセスのドメインでは AWSLambdaVPCAccessExecutionRole ポリシーが要ります。このポリシーが、Lambda が VPC の中の OpenSearch のエンドポイントへ書き込めるようにします。また、OpenSearch Service へ流せるのは Standard のログクラスのロググループだけです。

per_choice.A: 正しい。Lambda が VPC に入り、ドメインのエンドポイントへ書き込めるようになります。
per_choice.B: 正しい。OpenSearch Service へ流せるのは Standard のログクラスのロググループだけです。
per_choice.C: ドメインを作った後に、アクセスの種類は変えられません。
per_choice.D: サブスクリプションで送るログはもともと gzip で圧縮されており、届かない問題の原因ではありません。
per_choice.E: 実行ロールの信頼関係には lambda.amazonaws.com が必要です。

references.quote: It must have lambda.amazonaws.com in the trust relationship.
This Amazon-managed policy grants Lambda access to the customer's VPC, enabling Lambda to write to the OpenSearch endpoint in the VPC.
Streaming to OpenSearch Service is supported only for log groups in the Standard log class.
The domain can have either public access or VPC access, but you can't then modify the type of access after the domain is created.
